landing_page.py.title: Dear ImGui Bundle
landing_page.py.text:
*Interactive Python & C++ apps for desktop, mobile, and web - powered by [Dear
ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui).*
landing_page.py.summary: *Interactive Python & C++ apps for desktop, mobile, and web - powered by [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui).*

welcome_imm_mode.py.title: What is an Immediate GUI
welcome_imm_mode.py.text:
With [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), your GUI code is **simple and direct**: no widget trees,
no callbacks, no state synchronization. You call functions to create widgets, and they return the current
value. That's it.
welcome_imm_mode.py.summary: With [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), your GUI code is **simple and direct**: no widget trees, no callbacks, no state synchronization.

demo_hello_world.py.title: Hello world: a complete app in two lines of code.
demo_hello_world.py.text:
[ImmApp](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/core-libs/hello-imgui-immapp/) opens the window, runs the loop, and calls
your GUI function at every frame: `immapp.run(gui)` is all it takes. Add widgets to that function, and you have an
app. The C++ version is three lines.
demo_hello_world.py.summary: [ImmApp](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/core-libs/hello-imgui-immapp/) opens the window, runs the loop, and calls your GUI function at every frame: `immapp.run(gui)` is all it takes.

demo_parametric_curve.py.title: A parametric curve, and the immediate mode in a nutshell.
demo_parametric_curve.py.text:
Turn the knobs, or click **Random**: the curve follows at once. At every frame, the GUI function draws the plot with
[ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) and the knobs with
[imgui-knobs](https://github.com/altschuler/imgui-knobs), and reads their values right there. No callbacks, no widget
objects: that is the [immediate mode](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/intro/imm-gui/).
demo_parametric_curve.py.summary: Turn the knobs, or click **Random**: the curve follows at once.

demo_implot_markdown.py.title: An animated plot and some markdown, in a few lines.
demo_implot_markdown.py.text:
A cosine wave moves in an [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) plot, under a text written in
[markdown](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/addons/text-markdown/). Both are add-ons, activated in one call:
`immapp.run(gui, with_implot=True, with_markdown=True)`. A good start for a small app.
demo_implot_markdown.py.summary: A cosine wave moves in an [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) plot, under a text written in [markdown](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/addons/text-markdown/).

demo_assets_addons.py.title: Assets and add-ons: images, icons, markdown and plots.
demo_assets_addons.py.text:
Load images and icons from your [assets folder](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/python-assets/), and use
two add-ons: markdown and ImPlot. A markdown editor with a live preview, and a pie chart whose values you can drag.
Tick **More info** under each part to see how it is done. The add-ons are activated with `immapp.AddOnsParams`.
demo_assets_addons.py.summary: Load images and icons from your [assets folder](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/python-assets/), and use two add-ons: markdown and ImPlot.

haiku_implot_heart.py.title: A beating heart, in a few lines of ImPlot.
haiku_implot_heart.py.text:
A heart curve drawn with [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) beats at the rate set by a knob from
[imgui-knobs](https://github.com/altschuler/imgui-knobs). A few lines of Python: a parametric curve, scaled by a pulse
at each frame. Turn the knobs to change the heart rate, or its thickness.
haiku_implot_heart.py.summary: A heart curve drawn with [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot) beats at the rate set by a knob from [imgui-knobs](https://github.com/altschuler/imgui-knobs).

haiku_butterfly.py.title: Lorenz attractor and the butterfly effect
haiku_butterfly.py.text:
Two trajectories of the [Lorenz system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenz_system) start almost at the same point,
then drift apart: chaos in action. Drawn in 3D with [ImPlot3D](https://github.com/brenocq/implot3d). Sliders change
the system's parameters and the gap between the two starting points; Reset starts them over.
haiku_butterfly.py.summary: Two trajectories of the [Lorenz system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorenz_system) start almost at the same point, then drift apart: chaos in action.

explorables/julia_map.py.title: The Mandelbrot set as a map of Julia sets
explorables/julia_map.py.text:
Click a point of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) to see its [Julia
set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_set). Fly to famous values of c, and zoom into both pictures: near
each point, the two sets look alike.
explorables/julia_map.py.summary: Click a point of the [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set) to see its [Julia set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_set).

explorables/neural_spiral/neural_spiral..title: A tiny neural network learns two spirals
explorables/neural_spiral/neural_spiral..text:
Can 16 neurons tell two spirals apart? Watch a tiny [neural
network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(machine_learning)) learn, live, as in the [TensorFlow
Playground](https://playground.tensorflow.org). Then read how it works, formula by formula, next to its numpy
code.
explorables/neural_spiral/neural_spiral..summary: Can 16 neurons tell two spirals apart? Watch a tiny [neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network_(machine_learning)) learn, live, as in the [TensorFlow Playground](https://playground.tensorflow.org).

explorables/lesson_harmonic_motion.py.title: Simple harmonic motion
explorables/lesson_harmonic_motion.py.text:
A mass on a spring, a pendulum, a vibrating string: they all follow the same equation. It is the equation of
[simple harmonic motion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simple_harmonic_motion) (for the pendulum, at small
angles). Adjust the mass and the spring stiffness, and watch how the motion changes.
explorables/lesson_harmonic_motion.py.summary: A mass on a spring, a pendulum, a vibrating string: they all follow the same equation.

explorables/double_pendulum.py.title: Double Pendulum
explorables/double_pendulum.py.text:
A [double pendulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_pendulum) is a
[chaotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_theory) system: tiny changes in its initial conditions lead to
wildly different trajectories. Drag the angles to set initial positions, then release and watch chaos unfold.
explorables/double_pendulum.py.summary: A [double pendulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_pendulum) is a [chaotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaos_theory) system: tiny changes in its initial conditions lead to wildly different trajectories.

explorables/fourier_epicycles.py.title: Fourier Epicycles
explorables/fourier_epicycles.py.text:
Any closed curve can be approximated by a sum of rotating circles (a [Fourier
series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_series)). Adjust the number of circles to see how the
approximation improves.
explorables/fourier_epicycles.py.summary: Any closed curve can be approximated by a sum of rotating circles (a [Fourier series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourier_series)).

explorables/boids.py.title: Boids
explorables/boids.py.text:
A flock of birds emerges from three simple local rules, with no leader and no plan. Each bird stays apart
from its neighbors (**separation**), flies their way (**alignment**), and stays with them (**cohesion**).
This is the [boids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boids) model of Craig Reynolds (1986).
explorables/boids.py.summary: A flock of birds emerges from three simple local rules, with no leader and no plan.

explorables/logistic_map.py.title: Logistic Map
explorables/logistic_map.py.text:
A very simple equation, and yet it can lead to wildly different behaviors, up to chaos. The [logistic
map](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Logistic_map), `x(n+1) = r * x(n) * (1 - x(n))`, models for example the
*growth of a population with limited resources*. Depending on r, it is stable, periodic (in 2-cycles,
4-cycles, etc), or chaotic. Let's explore this.
explorables/logistic_map.py.summary: A very simple equation, and yet it can lead to wildly different behaviors, up to chaos.

layout_child.py.title: Resizable Layouts with begin_child
layout_child.py.text: Learn how to create resizable adjacent panels, using child windows.
layout_child.py.summary: Learn how to create resizable adjacent panels, using child windows.

layout_docking.py.title: Docking Layouts with Hello ImGui
layout_docking.py.text:
[Hello ImGui](https://github.com/pthom/hello_imgui) provides a **docking** system: define named dock spaces,
then assign windows to them.
Windows can be dragged, tabbed, and rearranged by the user.
layout_docking.py.summary: [Hello ImGui](https://github.com/pthom/hello_imgui) provides a **docking** system: define named dock spaces, then assign windows to them.

demo_docking.py.title: A full application: docking layouts, fonts, themes, logs and a status bar.
demo_docking.py.summary: A template for a real application, built with [Hello ImGui](https://pthom.github.io/hello_imgui/): copy it and start from there.

demo_custom_background.py.title: A 3D sea behind the GUI: a custom OpenGL background.
demo_custom_background.py.text:
Draw anything behind your GUI with OpenGL: here, an animated sea whose waves and colors you can tune. The [Seascape
shader](https://www.shadertoy.com/view/Ms2SD1) is by Alexander Alekseev (TDM, 2014). Hello ImGui calls
`runner_params.callbacks.custom_background` at each frame, before the GUI: that is where it draws, with OpenGL
([PyOpenGL](https://pypi.org/project/PyOpenGL/) in Python).
demo_custom_background.py.summary: Draw anything behind your GUI with OpenGL: here, an animated sea whose waves and colors you can tune.

demo_powersave.py.title: Power save: the app slows down when you don't use it.
demo_powersave.py.text:
When nothing happens, [Hello ImGui](https://pthom.github.io/hello_imgui/) lowers the frame rate to spare the CPU:
watch the FPS and the spinner slow down. Move the mouse, and they speed up again. The slider sets `fps_idle` (0 means
full speed), and the checkbox turns idling off, for example during an animation.
demo_powersave.py.summary: When nothing happens, [Hello ImGui](https://pthom.github.io/hello_imgui/) lowers the frame rate to spare the CPU: watch the FPS and the spinner slow down.

demo_chinese_font.py.title: Non-Latin text: Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Hebrew, Arabic
demo_chinese_font.py.text:
The bundled fonts cover Latin, Greek and Cyrillic only: other scripts show up as `???`. The fix: load a font that has
the glyphs you need, first, so that it becomes the default font. This demo shows how, with [Noto Sans
SC](https://fonts.google.com/noto/specimen/Noto+Sans+SC): download it, and the demo's sample lines come alive.
demo_chinese_font.py.summary: The bundled fonts cover Latin, Greek and Cyrillic only: other scripts show up as `???`.

demo_drag_and_drop.py.title: Drag and drop: copy, move or swap names between buttons.
demo_drag_and_drop.py.text:
Drag a name onto another button to copy it, move it, or swap the two: the radio buttons pick the mode. Each button is
both a drag source and a drop target. Adapted from the drag and drop section of the [Dear ImGui
demo](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui/blob/master/imgui_demo.cpp).
demo_drag_and_drop.py.summary: Drag a name onto another button to copy it, move it, or swap the two: the radio buttons pick the mode.

demo_command_palette.py.title: A command palette, as in VS Code or Sublime Text.
demo_command_palette.py.text:
A searchable list of commands, as in VS Code: press **Ctrl+Shift+P** (**Cmd+Shift+P** on macOS). Type a few letters
to filter it. One command changes the theme in two steps, another writes to the log below. Learn how to register
commands and their callbacks with [imgui-command-palette](https://github.com/hnOsmium0001/imgui-command-palette).
demo_command_palette.py.summary: A searchable list of commands, as in VS Code: press **Ctrl+Shift+P** (**Cmd+Shift+P** on macOS).

demo_testengine.py.title: Automate and test your app with ImGui Test Engine.
demo_testengine.py.text:
Three windows: the Dear ImGui demo, the [ImGui Test Engine](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui_test_engine) panel, and a
few buttons that run tests. Watch a test drive the mouse and the keyboard: it opens tree nodes, clicks buttons, types
text, and checks the results. See the [test engine doc](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/core-libs/test-engine/).
demo_testengine.py.summary: Three windows: the Dear ImGui demo, the [ImGui Test Engine](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui_test_engine) panel, and a few buttons that run tests.

demo_testapp.py.title: Drive an app from a script, and capture screenshots.
demo_testapp.py.text:
A test function drives the app: it clicks, moves a slider, opens a header, and takes a screenshot at each step.
`immapp.testing.run()` starts the app, runs the test function, then exits. Handy for automated checks and for
documentation pictures. See the [test engine doc](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/core-libs/test-engine/).
demo_testapp.py.summary: A test function drives the app: it clicks, moves a slider, opens a header, and takes a screenshot at each step.

imgui_demo.py.title: Dear ImGui: the full demo
imgui_demo.py.text:
Every widget and feature of [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), in Python. The reference to learn
Dear ImGui by example (a port of imgui_demo.cpp). Browse it next to its code in the [Dear ImGui
Explorer](https://pthom.github.io/imgui_explorer/?lib=imgui).
imgui_demo.py.summary: Every widget and feature of [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui), in Python.

implot_demo.py.title: ImPlot: the full demo
implot_demo.py.text:
Every kind of plot of [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot), in Python: lines, scatter, bars, heatmaps,
histograms, real-time plots and more. A port of implot_demo.cpp: browse it next to its code in the [Dear
ImGui Explorer](https://pthom.github.io/imgui_explorer/?lib=implot).
implot_demo.py.summary: Every kind of plot of [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot), in Python: lines, scatter, bars, heatmaps, histograms, real-time plots and more.

implot3d_demo.py.title: ImPlot3D: the full demo
implot3d_demo.py.text:
Rotatable, zoomable 3D plots in Python with [ImPlot3D](https://github.com/brenocq/implot3d): lines, scatter,
surfaces, meshes and more. A port of implot3d_demo.cpp: browse it next to its code in the [Dear ImGui
Explorer](https://pthom.github.io/imgui_explorer/?lib=implot3d).
implot3d_demo.py.summary: Rotatable, zoomable 3D plots in Python with [ImPlot3D](https://github.com/brenocq/implot3d): lines, scatter, surfaces, meshes and more.

immvision.py.title: ImmVision: Download & Inspect Images
immvision.py.text: [ImmVision](https://github.com/pthom/immvision) is an image debugger for Dear ImGui with zoom, pan, pixel inspection, and colormaps.
immvision.py.summary: [ImmVision](https://github.com/pthom/immvision) is an image debugger for Dear ImGui with zoom, pan, pixel inspection, and colormaps.

fiatlight_image.py.title: Fiatlight: Image Pipeline
fiatlight_image.py.text:
[Fiatlight](https://pthom.github.io/fiatlight/) turns Python functions into interactive apps with visual
pipelines.
fiatlight_image.py.summary: [Fiatlight](https://pthom.github.io/fiatlight/) turns Python functions into interactive apps with visual pipelines.

fiatlight_dataframe.py.title: Fiatlight: Titanic DataFrame Explorer
fiatlight_dataframe.py.text:
Explore the passengers of the Titanic in a **filterable dataframe**, with linked plots: filter them by class,
survival, sex and age, and watch the survival rate and the age histogram update. Built with
[Fiatlight](https://pthom.github.io/fiatlight), which turns Python functions into interactive apps with visual
pipelines.
fiatlight_dataframe.py.summary: Explore the passengers of the Titanic in a **filterable dataframe**, with linked plots: filter them by class, survival, sex and age, and watch the survival rate and the age histogram update.

themes.py.title: Theming
themes.py.text:
Pick a complete look for your app, then fine-tune its colors, rounding and spacing. The complete
looks come from [Hello ImGui](https://github.com/pthom/hello_imgui).
themes.py.summary: Pick a complete look for your app, then fine-tune its colors, rounding and spacing.

demo_widgets.py.title: Widgets: knobs, toggles, spinners and more
demo_widgets.py.text:
Knobs, toggle switches, spinners, a command palette, a dock-like cool bar: widgets beyond Dear ImGui's own. They come
from the libraries in the bundle: [imgui-knobs](https://github.com/altschuler/imgui-knobs),
[imgui_toggle](https://github.com/cmdwtf/imgui_toggle), [imspinner](https://github.com/dalerank/imspinner),
[imgui-command-palette](https://github.com/hnOsmium0001/imgui-command-palette) and ImCoolBar. Also file dialogs: the
native ones ([portable-file-dialogs](https://github.com/samhocevar/portable-file-dialogs)), and
[ImFileDialog](https://github.com/pthom/ImFileDialog), drawn with ImGui.
demo_widgets.py.summary: Knobs, toggle switches, spinners, a command palette, a dock-like cool bar: widgets beyond Dear ImGui's own.

demo_imgui_md.py.title: Markdown: a tour of rich_md
demo_imgui_md.py.text:
Markdown rendered in an ImGui window: styled text, tables, code, images, math, admonitions and more. Each section shows
its source, ready to copy. `rich_md` draws it directly, with no browser and no HTML engine.
demo_imgui_md.py.summary: Markdown rendered in an ImGui window: styled text, tables, code, images, math, admonitions and more.

demo_text_edit.py.title: Text editor: syntax highlighting, diffs, multiple cursors
demo_text_edit.py.text:
A code editor widget, with syntax highlighting, multiple cursors, a diff view, filters, annotations and context menus.
Each tab shows one feature, and a checkbox shows its source. The editor is
[ImGuiColorTextEdit](https://github.com/goossens/ImGuiColorTextEdit), by Johan A. Goossens.
demo_text_edit.py.summary: A code editor widget, with syntax highlighting, multiple cursors, a diff view, filters, annotations and context menus.

demo_logger.py.title: Logger: a log window for your app
demo_logger.py.text:
A log window for your app, with four levels: debug, info, warning and error. Call `hello_imgui.log()` anywhere, and
show the window with `hello_imgui.log_gui()`. Its colors follow the theme. Adapted from
[ImGuiAl](https://github.com/leiradel/ImGuiAl).
demo_logger.py.summary: A log window for your app, with four levels: debug, info, warning and error.

demo_terminal.py.title: Terminal: a shell inside an ImGui window
demo_terminal.py.text:
A real shell in an ImGui widget: type commands, scroll back through the history, select and copy. The shell runs
behind a pseudo-terminal (macOS and Linux), [pyte](https://github.com/selectel/pyte) parses its VT100 output, and
`imgui_bundle.imgui_terminal.TerminalView` draws it. A standalone version, with more comments:
`demos_terminal/demo_terminal_pyte.py`.
demo_terminal.py.summary: A real shell in an ImGui widget: type commands, scroll back through the history, select and copy.

demo_python_context_manager.py.title: Context managers for Dear ImGui and ImPlot in Python.
demo_python_context_manager.py.text:
In Python, `with imgui_ctx.begin("Window"):` replaces a `begin()` / `end()` pair, and the `end()` can no longer be
forgotten. The same exists for child windows, menus, popups, tables, tabs, fonts and styles, and for ImPlot with
`implot_ctx`. Open a section to try it and read its code. See the [Python
tips](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/python-tips/).
demo_python_context_manager.py.summary: In Python, `with imgui_ctx.begin("Window"):` replaces a `begin()` / `end()` pair, and the `end()` can no longer be forgotten.

demo_run_async.py.title: Run Python code alongside the GUI with immapp.run_async.
demo_run_async.py.text:
The GUI runs as an [asyncio](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html) task, while a Python loop keeps
computing. The window shows both rates: the GUI's frames per second, and the loop's computations per second. The loop
yields with `await asyncio.sleep(0)` to share the event loop. See [async
support](https://imgui-bundle.pages.dev/doc/python/python-async/).
demo_run_async.py.summary: The GUI runs as an [asyncio](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio.html) task, while a Python loop keeps computing.

demo_glfw_window_manip.py.title: Control the native window with GLFW: maximize, move, opacity.
demo_glfw_window_manip.py.text:
`glfw_utils.glfw_window_hello_imgui()` returns the [GLFW](https://www.glfw.org) window that Hello ImGui created. With
it, any function of [pyGLFW](https://github.com/FlorianRhiem/pyGLFW) works on your app's window. Here, buttons
maximize, restore, minimize or center it, a slider sets its opacity, and another button makes it ask for attention in
the taskbar.
demo_glfw_window_manip.py.summary: `glfw_utils.glfw_window_hello_imgui()` returns the [GLFW](https://www.glfw.org) window that Hello ImGui created.

demo_matplotlib.py.title: Matplotlib figures inside an ImGui window.
demo_matplotlib.py.text:
`imgui_fig.fig()` shows a [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org) figure as an image in the GUI. On the left, an animated
sine wave, redrawn at each frame, with a slider for its amplitude. On the right, a static figure, drawn once. Handy to
reuse existing Matplotlib code; for fast interactive plots, prefer [ImPlot](https://github.com/epezent/implot).
demo_matplotlib.py.summary: `imgui_fig.fig()` shows a [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org) figure as an image in the GUI.

demo_pydantic.py.title: ImVec2 and ImVec4 in Pydantic models.
demo_pydantic.py.text:
Save and load your app's settings with [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev), ImVec2 and colors included.
`ImVec2_Pydantic`, `ImVec4_Pydantic` and `ImColor_Pydantic` are the usual `ImVec2`, `ImVec4` and `ImColor`, usable as
fields of a Pydantic model. The demo shows such a model, turns it into JSON, validates it back, and checks that
nothing was lost.
demo_pydantic.py.summary: Save and load your app's settings with [Pydantic](https://docs.pydantic.dev), ImVec2 and colors included.

example_python_backend_glfw3.py.title: Dear ImGui in a window you own, with a pure Python backend: GLFW, SDL2, SDL3, pyglet, pygame or wgpu.
example_python_backend_glfw3.py.text:
Add ImGui to your own app: you write the app loop, and a Python backend does the rest. This one is for
[GLFW](https://www.glfw.org); the others (SDL2, SDL3, pyglet, pygame, wgpu) work the same way. The backend passes the
inputs to ImGui and draws it with PyOpenGL. Shows the ImGui demo, and a window with markdown and a formula. Needs
`pip install imgui-bundle[glfw,opengl]`.
example_python_backend_glfw3.py.summary: Add ImGui to your own app: you write the app loop, and a Python backend does the rest.

minimal_example.py.title: Deploy to the Web: Minimal HTML Example
minimal_example.py.text: Dear ImGui Bundle apps can run entirely in the browser using [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org). The HTML file below is a **complete, self-contained app** in about 80 lines - no server, no build step.
minimal_example.py.summary: Dear ImGui Bundle apps can run entirely in the browser using [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org).

webgl_minimal_mandelbrot.py.title: Minimal WebGL fragment shader as the application background.
webgl_minimal_mandelbrot.py.text:
The [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), drawn by a fragment shader behind the GUI.
**Pyodide only:** this demo calls the browser's
[WebGL2](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API) API directly, through Python's `js`
interop. On desktop, you would use PyOpenGL instead.
webgl_minimal_mandelbrot.py.summary: The [Mandelbrot set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandelbrot_set), drawn by a fragment shader behind the GUI.

webgl_background_shader.py.title: Custom background using a shader, à la Shadertoy
webgl_background_shader.py.text:
One source file, two platforms: a shader behind the GUI, with OpenGL on desktop and WebGL in the browser. The
shader is the famous "Seascape" from [Shadertoy](https://www.shadertoy.com/view/Ms2SD1), by Alexander
Alekseev. In the browser, the app runs with [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org).
webgl_background_shader.py.summary: One source file, two platforms: a shader behind the GUI, with OpenGL on desktop and WebGL in the browser.

webgl_texture_in_image.py.title: Render a 3D cube with WebGL from Python, and display it in an ImGui window
webgl_texture_in_image.py.text:
A 3D cube drawn with [WebGL2](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API) into a texture, and
shown in the GUI by `imgui.image()`. No copy between the GPU and the CPU at each frame.
webgl_texture_in_image.py.summary: A 3D cube drawn with [WebGL2](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebGL_API) into a texture, and shown in the GUI by `imgui.image()`.

webaudio_synth.py.title: WebAudio synthesizer: a piano, four tunes, and a scope.
webaudio_synth.py.text:
A small synthesizer written in Python: play the piano with the mouse or the computer keyboard, or let it play a
tune. Pick a waveform, add some echo, and watch the scope. **Pyodide only**: it plays through the browser's
[WebAudio API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Audio_API), via [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org)'s
`js` interop.
webaudio_synth.py.summary: A small synthesizer written in Python: play the piano with the mouse or the computer keyboard, or let it play a tune.
